extracted.intended_audience: investors, journalists, regulators, and the general public following corporate investigations
extracted.subtask_description: A public corporate/research-firm statement responding to a regulatory 'Show Cause' notice that defends an investigative report, rebuts alleged inaccuracies, and explains evidentiary and procedural context. Aimed at documenting facts, disclosures, and transparency for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-backed reporting / comprehensive citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should be supported by exhaustive primary and secondary evidence (e.g., Hindenburg's 106-page report with 32,000 words and 720 citations) tracing transactions, entities, and relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public documents, court and tribunal records, export/shipping records, audit correspondence, corporate filings, and interviews to substantiate claims; quantify scope (pages/words/citations) to demonstrate depth. Example: cite CESTAT, Supreme Court records, export documents, and audit issues when alleging related-party transactions or fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish primary documents / full disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Make primary source materials available in full (e.g., publish the entirety of a regulator's Show Cause Notice) so readers can evaluate the underlying record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to regulator notices, court orders, official filings, and other primary documents rather than summarizing selectively; publishing full notices guards against misinterpretation and increases transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of financial positions and investor relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any financial positions, short interests, and investor partnerships prominently (Hindenburg: 'we disclosed a short position in the very first line' and again at the end in big bold letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State ownership/position status at the start and end of a report, identify the number and nature of investor partners, and quantify gross/net gains where relevant to counter claims about motive or profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest and operational footprint disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare firm jurisdiction, registrations, local operations (or lack thereof), and any ties that could bear on jurisdictional claims or perceived bias (Hindenburg: 'a U.S.-based research firm with zero Indian entities, employees, consultants or operations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about where the firm is registered and whether it has local subsidiaries or personnel; disclose relationships with local brokers, banks, or other intermediaries that could be construed as links to the market under scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility and contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting potentially problematic or disfavored sources (e.g., a 'banned broker'), disclose their status and provide context so readers can assess reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label source limitations openly (e.g., banned, sanctioned, or litigated), explain why the source's information is still relevant, and present corroborating evidence where possible rather than concealing source defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration by independent media / third-party investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support investigative claims by citing independent media investigations and third-party reporting that corroborate or expand on findings (Hindenburg lists 40+ independent investigations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile and link to independent articles, investigations, and reports that confirm key elements; provide a timeline or rundown of corroborating pieces to demonstrate that allegations are not unilateral or isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology transparency (explain how conclusions reached)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe investigative methods used to trace networks, transactions, and related-party relationships (e.g., mapping offshore shell entities, tracing funds, reviewing related-party disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain steps taken: document analysis, entity linking, transactional tracing, interviews, cross-referencing regulator/audit records; make methodology clear so others can reproduce or assess the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official/regulatory/court records as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on and cite tribunal orders, regulator action records, audit opinions, and court filings (e.g., CESTAT orders, Supreme Court records, auditor resignations) when alleging wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary official sources for factual claims; when reporting on regulatory or judicial outcomes, quote the relevant passages and provide links or document references to the original orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful, defensible use of language (avoid unsupported sensationalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose adjectives and characterizations (e.g., 'scandal', 'leniency', 'sensationalized') that are defensible based on the evidence because regulators may allege 'sensationalizing' or 'distorting facts'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use strong descriptors when the factual record supports them; where a term could be challenged, provide definitional justification or evidence (e.g., show that penalties were reduced so 'leniency' is factually supported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-by-point rebuttal of regulatory allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When facing a regulator's notice, respond directly to specific alleged inaccuracies or technical points rather than only offering general defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each numbered allegation with the factual record, cite supporting documents, and explain why a regulatory interpretation is incorrect or why a technical complaint (e.g., about a disclaimer) is misplaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful drafting and clarity of disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft disclaimers to avoid misinterpretation (SEBI took issue with wording around 'presented as is' and claims of 'objectivity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plainly that material is opinion/investigative commentary, not investment advice; explain limitations of warranties and accuracy; avoid language that could be read as claiming absolute objectivity if that is not intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and jurisdictional clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the firm's legal status, registration, and the jurisdictional basis (or lack thereof) for regulatory claims against it (example: SEBI asserting jurisdiction over a U.S. firm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether you are subject to the regulator's rules, note where you are registered, and, if applicable, file requests for transparency (RTI/FOI) or legal challenges to overbroad jurisdictional assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations, risk statements, and encouragement of independent due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly warn readers that the report is not an investment recommendation and encourage them to perform their own due diligence and consult advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear risk-language, state 'use at your own risk' and 'consult financial, legal, and tax advisors' lines, and remind readers that opinions are subject to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose investigative costs and motives to counter profit-motive narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: State the financial reality of the investigation (e.g., net of costs the firm 'may barely come out above breakeven') to rebut claims the work was motivated solely by financial gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-level figures on revenue/gains and net economics of the investigation when relevant to public narratives about motive; be candid about non-financial motives like public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide event chronology and contextual background
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a timeline of publication, regulatory interactions, meetings, and subsequent developments (e.g., meetings between company executives and regulators, RTI filings) so readers can place allegations in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize context chronologically, note key dates (publication, regulator meetings, audits/resignations, corroborating investigations) and link to supporting records to help readers understand sequence and causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document auditor interactions and audit structure issues
rubrics_metrics.description: When alleging accounting or disclosure failures, document auditor relationships, resignations, and fragmented audit structures (Hindenburg cites Deloitte's resignation and ~40 different auditors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite auditor resignation letters, audit opinions, and fragmentation evidence; explain how audit structure or auditor conduct relates to the substance of alleged misstatements or related-party nondisclosures.
